clue.text: The French, following a plan, get shady trees

indicators.note: following places the French word after the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
les is the French plural form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A gardener consults a layout and plants trees that give shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shady' is literal here: the trees cast shade, nothing underhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Maples are broad-leaved trees whose canopies cast plenty of shade.

clue.text: Spread at sea to entrap fish

indicators.note: to entrap is to hold something within, so the fish goes inside

parts.note: marine means relating to the sea
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Fishermen spread nets on the ocean to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about nets; it is the noun for something put on bread. 'to entrap' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute you put on bread.

clue.text: Face pain with spirit

parts.note: pan is slang for the face
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Meeting suffering bravely.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence or verve.

clue.text: Given aid, created trouble and got out

indicators.note: letters put into trouble are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone given help only stirred things up and then left.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to root out entirely, removing or getting rid of something.

clue.text: Flag, as usual

explanation.surface: A banner that is entirely ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner carried on a pole, and standard also means normal or customary.

clue.text: Hill guide who causes much anguish

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a mentor is an adviser or guide

explanation.surface: A mountain guide makes the climbers suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts suffering on others is a persecutor.

clue.text: Home from one's travels

indicators.note: from tells you to take the letters out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A souvenir brought back after a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its home, and the word extends to any snug dwelling.

clue.text: Loving phone-call after a party

indicators.note: after places the call behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a ring is a telephone call in British usage

explanation.surface: A fond phone call the morning after a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep affection, worshipful fondness.

clue.text: Mother set about some soldiers -fancy!

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so the mother surrounds the soldiers

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A mum attacks a group of troops, how extraordinary!
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' reads as attacking, but here it means placed around. A dam is a mother in livestock breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to fancy or imagine it.

clue.text: New keys made for the island

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters come out freshly ordered

explanation.surface: A locksmith cuts fresh keys for an island home.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Conducted a bag search

parts.note: to have conducted a business is to have run it
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: Someone oversaw a check of a piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly and roughly, turning everything over.

clue.text: Revive with a little relaxation and a mineral

parts.note: a rest is a short spell of relaxation
ore is mineral-bearing rock that is mined

explanation.surface: A spa treatment promises renewal through a short break and some mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone is to bring them back to health or vigour.

clue.text: Cheers amid reform for a man of principle

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A principled reformer is greeted with applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician gave his name to a famous law of buoyancy, so he is literally known for a principle.

clue.text: Well-established business

explanation.surface: A company that has been around a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means solidly fixed or settled, and a firm is a company.

clue.text: Timekeeper is little help

parts.note: minute means tiny
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A small assistant keeps the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a clock face tracks the passing time.

clue.text: Country music composer

explanation.surface: A nation known for its traditional folk tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ireland was an English composer of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation west of Britain shares its name with the English composer John Ireland.

clue.text: Doesn't take into consideration special reductions

explanation.surface: A shopper ignores the sale prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount an idea is to disregard it, and discounts are price cuts.

clue.text: The outcome of pressure here will be a letting off

definitions.text: The outcome of pressure here will be a letting off

parts.words: The outcome of pressure here will be a letting off
parts.note: reads like forgiveness after pleading, but the pressure is a finger's squeeze and the letting off is a gun firing

explanation.surface: Under persuasion, someone will be excused punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing the lever on a firearm discharges it, which is letting it off.

clue.text: Having to do with jailed social worker being ashamed

parts.note: re means concerning or about
pent means shut up or confined
an ant is a social insect, a classic worker

explanation.surface: A guilty social worker locked up for a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a profession; it is the insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse for wrongdoing is contrition, sorrow for one's sins.

clue.text: Not interrupted without purpose

explanation.surface: A pointless activity carried on non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: without an end, that is, without an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken goes on for ever, and read as end-less it means having no goal.

clue.text: Shorten the time taken to provide port facilities

parts.note: to dock a tail is to cut it short
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Cutting the hours needed to build harbour amenities.
explanation.definitionFit: Dockage is the accommodation for ships at a quay, or the fee for using it.

clue.text: A neat drive

parts.note: reads like a tidy car journey or golf shot, but neat is an old word for cattle, so this is herding them together

explanation.surface: A tidy trip by car or a crisp golf shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, as in neat's-foot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering cattle together on horseback for counting or branding is a herding drive.

clue.text: Estate many men see split up

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number

indicators.note: to split something up breaks it apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of workers watch a country property being divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split up' rearranges MEN and SEE into EMESNE; Roman numerals let D stand for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor house and kept for the owner's use.

clue.text: With due deference for both state and church

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Being respectful towards both government and religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace, from Latin, is used before a name to mean with respect to someone you are disagreeing with.

clue.text: Over a quarter may be of imitation stone

parts.note: past means over, finished
E for east is one of the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: Something past its prime may be fake jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points N, S, E and W are each a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a glassy material used to make fake gems.

clue.text: Travel accompanied by a fellow worker

indicators.note: accompanied by sets the fellow alongside the travel word, following it

parts.note: to journey is to travel
a man is a fellow, a chap

explanation.surface: A colleague comes along on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman employed by another, a reliable working hand.

clue.text: Stood up for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman rises to her feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To have risen to one's feet is past tense of rise, and Rose is a girl's name.

clue.text: The attitude of people receiving one

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the people hold the one

parts.note: men stands for people generally
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The way a crowd behaves when welcoming someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or manner, which shows their outlook.

clue.text: Possibly it's not a stopping-place

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A doubt about whether somewhere is a place to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or bus stop where vehicles halt to pick up passengers is a stopping-place.

clue.text: Where to see a large bird by the water

indicators.note: by means next to, so the water comes beside the bird

parts.note: a swan is a big waterbird
the sea is the body of salt water

explanation.surface: Directions to a spot for watching a big bird beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh coastal city fits the whole picture: a place by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A place name answers the question of location, so a Welsh city is a fair 'where'.

clue.text: Late in the day the head makes a regular appearance

parts.note: even is a poetic word for evening
a ness is a headland or promontory on the coast

explanation.surface: A school principal turns up each evening without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland or promontory, as in Dungeness on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformity or steadiness of look is smoothness, a level, consistent quality.

clue.text: Coming nowadays before the opening

indicators.note: before puts the era abbreviation ahead of the opening

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
a vent is an opening that lets air out

explanation.surface: An arrival happening these days ahead of a grand launch.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, the coming of something important.
